fact_check.claim: 'KCC1, KCC2, and KCC20 are now final. Meaning they are ready for full adoption across the ecosystem... we invite Kaspa builders to join the public KCC channel' (transcript, Mike reading the announcement)
fact_check.verdict: verified verbatim and current: the KCC Coordination Forum announced on October 21, 2026 that 'KCC-1, KCC-2 and KCC-20 are now Final, meaning they are ready for full adoption across the ecosystem' and invited builders to 'join the public KCC channel to ask questions, get support, discuss implementations'. KCC-1 is the covenant specification, KCC-2 the authority (authorization) specification, KCC-20 the application standard for fungible-token covenants; under KCC-0, Final requires test vectors plus at least one public implementation that passes them (reference implementation in Argent with generated SilverScript contracts), and finalization does not change consensus rules or force adoption. Copy uses the quoted sentence, 'test vectors exist and a public implementation already passes them', and 'the public KCC channel' (platform not named by the source; the transcript's 'telegram' is not asserted).

fact_check.claim: 'KCC20... is built on covenants... released like a month or two ago... tokens etched into the L1 rather than through a third party indexer like Kasplex' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in substance, dates made precise: covenants activated on Kaspa mainnet with the Toccata upgrade on June 30, 2026 (prior ledger, was-i-right), so copy says 'covenants went live with Toccata at the end of June' rather than 'a month or two ago'. KRC-20 token ownership 'isn't enforced directly by Kaspa consensus'; the off-chain Kasplex indexer reads KRC-20 instructions embedded in Kaspa transactions and determines ownership, while KCC-20 is 'a standard designed to put token rules into scripts enforced by the network itself'. Copy: 'a third-party indexer reading the chain', 'rules in covenants on the Kaspa L1 itself, enforced by the network'.

fact_check.claim: The September 20 KRC-20 indexer exploit (NOT in the transcript; added as the verified illustration of the middleman risk Mike described)
fact_check.verdict: verified: on September 20, 2026 an attacker used an empty signature plus an OP_NOT after OP_ENDIF so the base chain accepted the script while the Kasplex indexer credited five forged KRC-20 transfers (about 186.4M ZEAL and 54.4B NACHO from a bridge custody address); the forged tokens were minted on the L2s and sold into Zealous Swap pools, which lost 94% to 99.6% of their KAS-side value; the article states Kaspa itself was not hacked and native KAS and Kaspa consensus were unaffected. Copy keeps it to one beat: 'a month ago that indexer got tricked into crediting forged transfers and two token pools got drained. Kaspa itself was never hacked', and the V4 slide 3 figures '94% to 99.6%'.

fact_check.claim: 'look who responded. Nacho the cat. Excited for our future on Kaspa. Who's with us? Migration to KCC20 is up next to be announced... the KRC20s have to migrate over to KCC20' (transcript, Mike reading a Nacho post)
fact_check.verdict: verified in the general form only: Bitcoin.com (September 21) reports Nacho the Kat 'says the community intends to move toward KCC-20'; a KuCoin item reports KaspaCom building a one-way bridge to move KRC20 and Kaspa L2 tokens onto KCC-20 (prior ledger). The exact post wording Mike read on stream is not indexed anywhere I could reach, so copy never quotes it and says 'Nacho the Kat already said the community is moving over to KCC-20' and 'the ecosystem is building the bridges'. 'Have to migrate' is softened to 'the migration is next'. Nacho is described as 'one of the OG KRC20s' (launched on KRC20 in 2024, named after Kaspa core dev Shai Wyborski's cat); 'biggest KRC20' is not claimed (NACHO market cap about $4M, CoinGecko).

fact_check.claim: 'demands for KRC20s were pretty high back in 2024'; KRC20 went live in 2024 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: KRC20 went live on Kaspa mainnet September 15, 2024 (prior ledger). Copy: 'Back in 2024 the demand for KRC20s was through the roof' (Mike's read) and the V4 slide 2 milestone 'KRC20 LIVE: SEPT 2024'.

fact_check.claim: 'U.S. officially finalizes crypto stablecoin regulations under the Genius Act' (transcript, reading a headline)
fact_check.verdict: verified and made precise: the OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rule on October 21, 2026, the first federal regulator to finish; both the rule and the Act take effect January 18, 2027; issuers must hold reserves at least equal to outstanding stablecoins and generally process redemptions within two business days; the ban on paying yield directly to holders stays (the proposed affiliate presumption was dropped). Copy: 'The OCC just finalized the GENIUS Act stablecoin rules: full reserves, redemptions within two business days, live January 18, 2027'. 'The US is shifting the dollar's backing from oil to the stablecoin' is Mike's own on-stream read, written as 'the way I see it'.

fact_check.claim: 'we have a hawkish Fed chair, Kevin Warsh... the entire market believes there's not going to be a rate hike... 86% chance that interest rates are not going to change... October 28... I think it's more likely than not that we're going to get a rate hike' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: the FOMC meets October 27-28, 2026 (target range 3.75% to 4.00% after Chair Warsh's September hike, a 12-0 vote); CME FedWatch on October 21 prices roughly 16% for a quarter-point hike and about 84% for a hold (17% on rateprobability.com), after a spike to about 41% to 44% on the hot September CPI (October 14) and a fall-back after Warsh declined to signal in Bangkok; CNBC ran 'Everyone expects the Fed to hold rates in October. Kevin Warsh could surprise us all' (October 16). Copy says 'about 84%' / 'about 84% of traders price a pause' and 'a chair who already hiked in September'. The hike call is Mike's own, in first person, with 'never financial advice' kept in the YT post.

Copy does not name him (he anchored the downtober V4 carousel a week ago); it says 'the May high it was never supposed to take out'.

fact_check.claim: 'back in 2022... we went down to 15,600... everybody and their grandma believes Bitcoin was going to go down to 8k but it didn't happen, bear trap... eight weeks later we're just going back up' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified with the numbers corrected: the November 2022 low was $15,476 (November 21, 2022, after the FTX collapse); contemporaneous calls were for $10,000 (crypto Twitter) with bearish targets as low as $6,000 (ZebPay, November 28, 2022); no verifiable $8,000 call surfaced, so copy says 'calling $10K. Some were calling $6K'. Eight weeks after the low (mid-January 2023) Bitcoin was above $21K and January 2023 closed up about 40%, so 'eight weeks later it was ripping' and 'then a 40% January' (quiz 2) hold. 'Bear trap' is Mike's characterization, kept in his voice.

yt_posts.body:
KCC-1, KCC-2 and KCC-20 are FINAL. Kaspa's native token standard is ready for full adoption, and the KRC20 migration is next.

Here is what actually changed, and why it matters more than the price move.

On October 21 the KCC Coordination Forum declared all three standards Final: KCC-1 is the covenant spec, KCC-2 is the authorization spec, and KCC-20 is the fungible token standard built on top of them. Final means the test vectors exist and a public implementation already passes them. Builders are invited into the public KCC channel to ship on it.

Why does this matter? Think about how KRC20 worked. Your token balance was never enforced by Kaspa consensus; a third-party indexer read instructions off the chain and decided who owned what. A month ago that indexer got tricked into crediting forged transfers and two token pools got drained. Kaspa itself was never hacked. That is the middleman risk.

KCC-20 tokens keep their rules in covenants on the Kaspa L1 itself. Covenants went live with Toccata at the end of June. The network enforces the rules, not somebody's server. The tokens are etched into the L1.

So the migration is the next story. Nacho the Kat, one of the OG KRC20s, already said the community is moving over to KCC-20, and the ecosystem is building the bridges. Which tokens move first, and how fast, is what I am watching now.

And here is the part I like most: there is no reason to say "KRC20 token" or "KCC-20 token" anymore. The same way you say Solana tokens, now you just say Kaspa tokens. Open the wallet, select Kaspa as the network, swap. Back in 2024 the demand for KRC20s was through the roof. Native tokens on the fastest proof-of-work L1 around should pull even more.

$KAS is at about 3.9 cents this week, up on the news and still about 80% under its all-time high. The tech keeps shipping while the price sleeps.

yt_posts.body:
Everybody is pricing a Fed pause on October 28. I think it is more likely than not that Warsh hikes, and I think the dump that follows is a bear trap.

Here is the setup, the 2022 parallel, and exactly what I do if it plays out.

Start with the market. About 84% of traders price a pause. Hot CPI, hot PPI, the ISM prices index at 77.9, and a chair who already hiked in September. I keep asking what data people are looking at that says pause, and nobody can tell me. When everybody prices a pause and gets a hike, nobody is positioned for it, and everything goes down, down, down.

Now the chart. $BTC is at about $83K, riding the 50-day SMA (about $81.7K) as support, hanging around the May high it was never supposed to take out. The 50-week SMA sits at about $76K. A hike probably takes us there. That is a 7% to 8% drop, not the end of the world.

Here is the 2022 parallel. In November 2022 Bitcoin printed $15.5K, and everybody and their grandma was calling $10K. Some called $6K. The bears were certain the floor was gone. Eight weeks later Bitcoin was ripping and it never looked back. Classic bear trap: the drop that convinces the bears it keeps falling, right before it reverses.

Same shape here. If we tumble to the 50-week SMA, the bears will scream "told you so" and the four-year cycle zombies will panic about their October bottom. Meanwhile the economy is in expansion (ISM PMI at 54.5, nine months in a row), the OCC just finalized the GENIUS Act stablecoin rules, and after the midterms on November 3 things typically get better no matter who wins.

So the plan: I DCA a little now, because you cannot wait for a crash that may never come. If the hike lands and we hit the 50-week SMA, I buy everything on my list. And if the Fed pauses after all, it is not a god candle; it just means we may never test the 50-week at all, and we grind higher from here.

Never financial advice. I could be wrong, and that is the whole point of a bear trap: the people who are sure are the ones who get caught.
